section_summary: This section concludes a report on Japan’s automotive industry in 1939. It describes restrictions on American imports, expansion of Japanese manufacturing, exports of replacement parts, charcoal fuel policies, and the military’s influence on production. A final confidential page identifies four sources used in the report.

subfiles.title: Report on the Japanese automotive industry
subfiles.about: The report assesses Japan’s expanding domestic automotive industry and the prospects for American automobile and parts exports.
subfiles.summary: The report says foreign exchange restrictions have sharply reduced American car imports while officials encourage limited German imports and expand Japanese factories across Japan and the Asian continent. It describes growing exports of Japanese replacement parts, government pressure to convert vehicles to charcoal fuel, and military demand for trucks and better parts. Despite the perceived quality advantage of American vehicles, the author expects Japanese production and restrictions on imports to end American dominance of Japan’s automotive market.

subfiles.title: Sources of Information—Strictly Confidential
subfiles.about: The list identifies four industry sources and warns that disclosure would harm their standing in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Names four confidential automotive industry sources and urges secrecy.
